summary: Know that coins and bills are money, and name the values of all U.S. coins and the $1 bill.
Compare the values of coins and dollar bills, and write amounts with the ¢ and $ signs.
Solve money problems up to $20 and show the same amount in different ways.
Know that people collect data to answer questions, and that data can vary.
Identify what can count as data, such as pictures, sounds and numbers.
Solve two-step word problems with all four operations, including money; check with estimation.
Write questions that data can answer and decide what data to collect.
Collect class data, or use existing data, to answer a data question.
Create, explore and refine questions that data can answer.
Plan how to collect different kinds of data and organize it digitally.
Understand that part of a data set can be selected and analyzed for a purpose.
Analyze charts of one data set, explain them, and draw conclusions the data supports.
See how different charts highlight different sides of data, and describe patterns in them.
Collect, organize and display data from various sources, and share results digitally.
Collect and clean data, fixing formatting and handling missing entries.
Use double line plots or double bar graphs to compare data across samples.

state_code: # SOURCES (New Jersey Student Learning Standards - Mathematics, adopted 4 Oct 2023; districts had to align by September 2025)
# - NJ codes keep CCSS cluster letters (e.g. 3.NF.A.2a); the crosswalk codes sub-parts separately, so each lettered sub-part gets a row.
# - The K-5 Measurement and Data (MD) domain is split into Measurement (M) and Data Literacy (DL); those standards are renumbered but their text is
#   unchanged from CCSS (crosswalk type "Indicator"), so they are "same" with the old MD code in ccss.
# CCSS K-5 STANDARDS DROPPED: none. Every non-MD CCSS K-5 code keeps its code in NJ, and every MD standard is re-coded under M or DL.
# - "Fluently" became "with accuracy and efficiency" (K.OA.A.5, 1.OA.C.6, 2.OA.B.2, 2.NBT.B.5, 3.OA.C.7, 4.NBT.B.4, 5.NBT.B.5); treated as "same".
# - Added worked examples or clarifications (e.g. 2.G.A.3, 3.NF.A.1-3, 3.M.A.2) are treated as "same"; 3.OA.D.8 adds money problems and is "edited".
# - The new money standards K.M.B.3, 1.M.C.4 and 1.M.C.5 are labelled "New" by NJ; here they are "moved" with 2.MD.C.8 (the CCSS money standard). Judgement call.
# - The 2016 NJSLS-M (baseline of NJ's crosswalk) was assumed to match CCSS codes; the 2023 text was also compared to CCSS directly.
# - CCSS baseline: CCSS Math PDF, https://corestandards.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Math_Standards1.pdf ; ccss codes are expanded with cluster letters from the CCSS K-5 list.
# - kind is judged on content, not code: a state standard that only renames/recodes or drops/moves examples into notes is "same".
# - Lettered sub-parts get their own row (with a stem row when the stem has its own text). A sub-part that mirrors a CCSS sub-part is "same";
#   a sub-part carved out of a CCSS standard that has no such sub-part (e.g. a split of one CCSS sentence into a/b) is "edited" with a summary.
# - Sub-part rows list the parent CCSS code (CCSS sub-part letters are not used in the ccss column).
# - "moved" is used when the main content comes from another CCSS grade; the other grade's code is in ccss.
